blocks.content: The REST API module connects Qprovement to external data sources. It performs HTTP GET requests against a URL, shows the response for inspection, and can repeat the fetch on a schedule — e.g. to regularly poll measurements from a server, a machine controller, or a cloud service. Mappings of individual fields of the response to worksheet columns can already be defined; they are stored but not applied yet — a fetch writes nothing into the worksheet today.
A saved entry with name, URL, optional HTTP headers, column mappings, write mode and schedule. Any number of endpoints can be managed per project — e.g. one per machine or per data source.
A dot notation that addresses a specific value or array in the API response (e.g. data.measurements or result.values[*].temperature). The value behind this path is meant for the assigned column.
A list of assignments: each entry maps one JSON path to one target column in the worksheet; within an endpoint a column belongs to at most one mapping. The mappings are stored but not applied yet.
Defines how the mapped values are to be written into the columns — clear columns before writing, append data at the end, or insert data at the top. The mode is stored but not applied yet.

Optional repeating fetch in minutes or hours (1 to 999). As long as the module is open and a URL is set, it automatically calls the endpoint at the configured interval. Only one fetch runs at a time; a fetch that falls due during a running one is skipped.

items: Use "+" to create a new endpoint and give it a meaningful name.
Enter the URL — typically a REST interface that returns JSON.
Add HTTP headers if needed (e.g. Authorization for API keys or bearer tokens).
Click "Send" to run a test fetch — the response is displayed for inspection. A running fetch can be stopped with "Cancel".
Identify JSON paths in the response and assign each one to a column (stored, but not applied yet).
Pick the write mode: clear, append at the end, or insert at the top (stored, but not applied yet).
Optional: enable the schedule and enter an interval in minutes or hours.
Deleting an endpoint automatically stops a running schedule.
Only one fetch runs at a time, across endpoints too; "Send" is disabled while one is running.
The full state (endpoints, headers, mappings, schedules) is included in the project export; responses are not.

blocks.content: The app only allows requests to its own origin. An address on another server fails in the browser before reaching the network and shows as status 0 with the error message. Remedy: serve the data through your own server (e.g. a proxy).

API keys, bearer tokens, and passwords are stored in clear text in the project in the browser so that the fetch can send them. Values of secret headers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, X-API-Key and any name containing token, secret, key or auth) appear only as •••• in the project export and when an agent reads. An imported project loads these values empty; the module lists the missing credentials, which must be entered again. Other headers are exported unchanged.
If the server declares JSON as content type but sends invalid content, status 0 appears with the parser message; the actual status of the response is not visible then.
Typos or the wrong nesting depth make a mapping point at nothing. Check the path against the response of a test fetch.

Once mappings are applied, the mode "Clear columns before writing" overwrites the column content on every scheduled fetch — old values would be lost. For time series, choose "Append data at the end". Today nothing is written yet.

blocks.term: Schedule only runs while the module is open
blocks.content: The recurring fetch runs in the browser tab. Closing the module or the browser stops the schedule. For real background acquisition, a server-side job is required.
